detail.longDescription: Of late, there has been a surge of interest amongst # IT coders to learn esoteric # programming languages, like BF, WS, etc. All learning is good investment. But there is only so much time one could invest into such endeavours. In my view, those who have a taste for the uncommon should, instead, study Forth, Smalltalk, Prolog, Scheme, Erlang, Eiffel, J, Figaro, FAUST, and loads of other practical GPLs. An even better investment of their time is for these kids to study mathematical logic, computability theory, complexity theory, category theory, formal languages, and type theories. An IT practitioner with a strong CS theoretical foundation—now, that is the "uncommon" of a higher order.
